 module DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-SPEC
   imports DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-VERIFICATION
 
+  claim [loop-invariant]:
+    <k>
+      #loop(
+        list(numVals(NUMBERS)),
+        Name("number"),
+        If(
+          BoolOp(
+            "and",
+            Call(
+              Name("isinstance"),
+              Name("number"),
+              Name("int")),
+            Compare(
+              Name("number"),
+              CmpOp(">", Int(0))),
+            Compare(
+              BinOp("%", Name("number"), Int(2)),
+              CmpOp("==", Int(1)))),
+          AugAssign(
+            Name("total"),
+            "+",
+            BinOp("**", Name("number"), Int(2))),
+          .Stmts))
+      ~> Return(Name("total"))
+      ~> #endcall
+    =>
+      ACC +Int doubleDifferenceSpec(NUMBERS)
+      ~> CONT
+    </k>
+    <env> LOCAL => CALLER </env>
+    <scopes>
+      (LOCAL |-> scope(
+        "total" |-> ACC
+        LOCALS,
+        PARENT)
+       SCOPES)
+    =>
+      SCOPES
+    </scopes>
+    <scopeLoc> LOCAL +Int 1 => LOCAL </scopeLoc>
+    <heap> HEAP </heap>
+    <heapLoc> NEXTHEAP </heapLoc>
+    <stack>
+      ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLER, LOCAL)) STACK
+    =>
+      STACK
+    </stack>
+    <ret> noRet </ret>
+    <exc> NoExc </exc>
+    <exit-code> 0 </exit-code>
+
   claim [double-the-difference-correct]:

module DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-VERIFICATION
  imports MPY

  // A symbolic sequence of exactly the numeric values admitted by the prompt.
  // Keeping the Int/Float choice in the constructor lets kprove split the
  // sequence structurally instead of treating an arbitrary Val as non-integer.
  syntax NumSeq ::= ".NumSeq"
                  | iNum(Int, NumSeq)
                  | fNum(Float, NumSeq)

  // numVals is a proof-domain representation of a list's ValSeq.  Its iterator
  // rules expose the NumSeq constructor directly to symbolic narrowing.
  syntax ValSeq ::= numVals(NumSeq)
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(numVals(.NumSeq)))
        => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(numVals(iNum(I, REST))))
        => #iterYield(I, list(numVals(REST))) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(numVals(fNum(F, REST))))
        => #iterYield(F, list(numVals(REST))) ... </k>

  rule oddSquare(I)
    => #if I >Int 0 andBool pyMod(I, 2) ==Int 1
       #then I *Int I
       #else 0
       #fi

  rule doubleDifferenceSpec(.NumSeq)       => 0
  rule doubleDifferenceSpec(iNum(I, REST))
    => oddSquare(I) +Int doubleDifferenceSpec(REST)
  rule doubleDifferenceSpec(fNum(_F, REST))
    => doubleDifferenceSpec(REST)

  syntax Val ::= finalNumber(NumSeq, Val) [function, total]
  rule finalNumber(.NumSeq, OLD)          => OLD
  rule finalNumber(iNum(I, REST), _OLD)   => finalNumber(REST, I)
  rule finalNumber(fNum(F, REST), _OLD)   => finalNumber(REST, F)

#!/usr/bin/env bash

  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \

  --backend haskell \
  --main-module DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-VERIFICATION \
  --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \

kprove spec.k \
  --definition verification-kompiled \
  --spec-module DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-SPEC

requires "reference-semantics/semantics.k"

module DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-VERIFICATION
  imports MPY

  // A symbolic sequence of exactly the numeric values admitted by the prompt.
  // Keeping the Int/Float choice in the constructor lets kprove split the
  // sequence structurally instead of treating an arbitrary Val as non-integer.
  syntax NumSeq ::= ".NumSeq"
                  | iNum(Int, NumSeq)
                  | fNum(Float, NumSeq)

  // numVals is a proof-domain representation of a list's ValSeq.  Its iterator
  // rules expose the NumSeq constructor directly to symbolic narrowing.
  syntax ValSeq ::= numVals(NumSeq)
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(numVals(.NumSeq)))
        => #iterDone ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(numVals(iNum(I, REST))))
        => #iterYield(I, list(numVals(REST))) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterNext(list(numVals(fNum(F, REST))))
        => #iterYield(F, list(numVals(REST))) ... </k>

  syntax Int ::= oddSquare(Int) [function, total]
  rule oddSquare(I)
    => #if I >Int 0 andBool pyMod(I, 2) ==Int 1
       #then I *Int I
       #else 0
       #fi

  syntax Int ::= doubleDifferenceSpec(NumSeq) [function, total]
  rule doubleDifferenceSpec(.NumSeq)       => 0
  rule doubleDifferenceSpec(iNum(I, REST))
    => oddSquare(I) +Int doubleDifferenceSpec(REST)
  rule doubleDifferenceSpec(fNum(_F, REST))
    => doubleDifferenceSpec(REST)

  syntax Val ::= finalNumber(NumSeq, Val) [function, total]
  rule finalNumber(.NumSeq, OLD)          => OLD
  rule finalNumber(iNum(I, REST), _OLD)   => finalNumber(REST, I)
  rule finalNumber(fNum(F, REST), _OLD)   => finalNumber(REST, F)
endmodule
requires "verification.k"

module DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-SPEC
  imports DOUBLE-THE-DIFFERENCE-VERIFICATION

  claim [loop-invariant]:
    <k>
      #loop(
        list(numVals(NUMBERS)),
        Name("number"),
        If(
          BoolOp(
            "and",
            Call(
              Name("isinstance"),
              Name("number"),
              Name("int")),
            Compare(
              Name("number"),
              CmpOp(">", Int(0))),
            Compare(
              BinOp("%", Name("number"), Int(2)),
              CmpOp("==", Int(1)))),
          AugAssign(
            Name("total"),
            "+",
            BinOp("**", Name("number"), Int(2))),
          .Stmts))
      ~> CONT
    =>
      CONT
    </k>
    <env> 1 </env>
    <scopes>
      1 |-> scope(
        "lst" |-> _INPUT
        "total" |->
          (ACC => ACC +Int doubleDifferenceSpec(NUMBERS))
        "number" |->
          (OLDNUMBER => finalNumber(NUMBERS, OLDNUMBER)),
        parent(0))
      0 |-> scope(
        "double_the_difference" |-> _FUNCTION,
        parent(-1))
      -1 |-> builtinsScope
    </scopes>

  claim [double-the-difference-correct]:
    <k>
      Call(
        Name("double_the_difference"),
        list(numVals(NUMBERS)))
      => doubleDifferenceSpec(NUMBERS)
    </k>
    <env> 0 </env>
    <scopes>
      0 |-> scope(
        "double_the_difference" |->
          closureVal(
            "lst",
            Assign(Name("total"), Int(0))
            Assign(Name("number"), Int(0))
            For(
              Name("number"),
              Name("lst"),
              If(
                BoolOp(
                  "and",
                  Call(
                    Name("isinstance"),
                    Name("number"),
                    Name("int")),
                  Compare(
                    Name("number"),
                    CmpOp(">", Int(0))),
                  Compare(
                    BinOp("%", Name("number"), Int(2)),
                    CmpOp("==", Int(1)))),
                AugAssign(
                  Name("total"),
                  "+",
                  BinOp("**", Name("number"), Int(2))),
                .Stmts))
            Return(Name("total")),
            0),
        parent(-1))
      -1 |-> builtinsScope
    </scopes>
    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    <heap> .Map </heap>
    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    <stack> .List </stack>
    <ret> noRet </ret>
    <exc> NoExc </exc>
    <exit-code> 0 </exit-code>
endmodule

# Trust-boundary discovery

The canonical inventory identifies 10 rules in the local verification-module closure. Each appears exactly once in `trust-boundary.json`, in canonical inventory order.

## Operational rules

The three `#iterNext(list(numVals(...)))` rules are classified as `OPERATIONAL_RULE`. Together they give the verification model's proof-domain list representation its ordinary MPY iterator behavior:

- the empty representation produces `#iterDone`;
- an integer-headed representation yields the integer and its tail;

These rules describe how the modeled input is executed and observed. They are not additional arithmetic or logical facts.

The other seven rules are classified as `DEFINITION`:

- `oddSquare` defines the per-integer contribution;
- the three `doubleDifferenceSpec` equations define the recursive result summary for empty, integer-headed, and float-headed sequences;
- the three `finalNumber` equations define the final value of the Python loop-target local for the same sequence cases.
